title: `DELETE RETURNING` and `UPDATE RETURNING` CTEs no longer compile with ORM API in SQLAlchemy 2.0

labels.name: regression
labels.description: something worked and was broken by a change

labels.name: great mcve
labels.description: An issue with a great mcve

labels.name: near-term release
labels.description: addition to the milestone which indicates this should be in a near-term release

body:
### Describe the bug

After upgrading to SQLAlchemy 2.0 from 1.4 according to the [Major Migration Guide](https://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/20/changelog/migration_20.html), all my queries that `select` from CTEs consisting of `update().returning()` and `delete().returning()` no longer compile. At the same time, `insert().returning()` and `select()` CTEs continue to work as expected.

The compile failure can be triggered both using `print(query)` and `.execute(query)`, and the database driver does not appear to be relevant.

I'm using the ORM API to define my tables. The bug does not occur with the Core API.

### Optional link from https://docs.sqlalchemy.org which documents the behavior that is expected

_No response_

### SQLAlchemy Version in Use

2.0.13

### DBAPI (i.e. the database driver)

asyncpg

### Database Vendor and Major Version

PostgreSQL 14

### Python Version

3.10

### Operating system

Linux

### To Reproduce

```python
from sqlalchemy import (
    delete,
    Column,
    Integer,
    MetaData,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base

meta = MetaData()
Base = declarative_base(metadata=meta)


class T1(Base):
    __tablename__ = "t1"
    id = Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True)


cte_delete = delete(T1).returning(T1.id).cte("delete_t1")
query = cte_delete.select()
print(query)

```

### Additional context

The snippet below provides more examples and a comparison with the Core API behavior:

<details>
<summary>orm_vs_core.py</summary>

```py
import sqlalchemy.exc
from sqlalchemy import (
    insert,
    select,
    update,
    delete,
    Column,
    Integer,
    MetaData,
    Table,
)
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base

meta = MetaData()
Base = declarative_base(metadata=meta)

print("=== ORM API ===")


class T1(Base):
    __tablename__ = "t1"
    id = Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True)


cte_delete = delete(T1).returning(T1.id).cte("delete_t1")
query1 = cte_delete.select()
try:
    print(query1)
except sqlalchemy.exc.CompileError as e:
    print("1. CTEs with DELETE RETURNING don't work")
    print("Error:", e)
    print()

cte_update = update(T1).returning(T1.id).cte("update_t1")
query2 = cte_update.select()
try:
    print(query2)
except sqlalchemy.exc.CompileError as e:
    print("2. CTEs with UPDATE RETURNING don't work")
    print("Error:", e)
    print()

print("3. CTEs with INSERT RETURNING work")
cte_insert = insert(T1).returning(T1.id).cte("insert_t1")
query3 = cte_insert.select()
print(query3)
print()

print("4. CTEs with SELECT work")
cte_select = select(T1.id).cte("delete_t1")
query4 = cte_select.select()
print(query4)
print()

print("=== Core API ===")
T2 = Table(
    "t2",
    meta,
    Column("id", Integer, primary_key=True),
)

print("1. Core CTEs with DELETE RETURNING work")
cte_delete = delete(T2).returning(T2.c.id).cte("delete_t2")
query1 = cte_delete.select()
print(query1)
print()

print("2. Core CTEs with UPDATE RETURNING work")
cte_update = update(T2).returning(T2.c.id).cte("update_t2")
query2 = cte_update.select()
print(query2)
print()

print("3. CORE CTEs with INSERT RETURNING work")
cte_insert = insert(T2).returning(T2.c.id).cte("insert_t2")
query3 = cte_insert.select()
print(query3)
print()

print("4. CORE CTEs with SELECT work")
cte_select = select(T2.c.id).cte("select_t2")
query4 = cte_select.select()
print(query4)
```
